_meta.purpose: Every number published anywhere on this site lives here and nowhere else. Prose renders numbers only via the {% metric %} shortcode, which throws at build on an unknown key. That is the point: a wrong number should be un-typeable, not merely discouraged.
_meta.source: career-os/vault/metrics.md and projects.md. The `source` field on each entry cites the vault ID so a claim can be traced back in one hop.

confidenceRendering.projection: prefixed 'an estimated'; a visible `footnote` is MANDATORY and the build fails without one

_meta.displayRule: `display` carries the bare figure with no hedging words. The shortcode adds the hedge from `confidence`. Do not pre-hedge a display string or it will read 'roughly roughly'.

attributionRendering.team: renders 'built by <credit>; my role was <role>' — never presentable as a personal achievement

_meta.publishRule: `publish: false` means the number is recorded for provenance but must never reach built HTML. tests/content-consistency.spec.js greps the build for the literals in `_superseded`.

experience_years.note: String, never a number. A build assertion enforces the type — a float here silently becomes '4.5' and drops the '+'.

golden_dataset_india_mh.label: Golden-dataset cases gating every India Maternal Health release
golden_dataset_india_mh.basis: 303 clinical (130 English + 98 Hindi + 75 Assamese) + 48 adversarial/safety. Counted from the versioned golden-dataset JSON in git.
golden_dataset_india_mh.scopeNote: India Maternal Health only — the one RAG program. The HPV datasets evaluate intent classification and Smart Snippets, not retrieval, and are counted separately.

golden_dataset_hpv.unit: curated cases per HPV program (Indonesia · India · Thailand)
golden_dataset_hpv.basis: Counted from the versioned golden-dataset JSON in git.

nightly_eval_cost.unit: USD of judge-model API spend per nightly run
nightly_eval_cost.label: Cost of the full nightly evaluation
nightly_eval_cost.basis: Derived from LLM API billing across judge-model configurations, not a reconciled invoice line item.
nightly_eval_cost.scopeNote: The saving is what paid for coverage: the nightly job went from a 60-case sample to the full 351-case dataset.

prompt_review_time.unit: reviewer time per prompt version bump
prompt_review_time.label: Prompt-regression review per version
prompt_review_time.basis: PR review timestamps before and after the snapshot suite landed.
prompt_review_time.scopeNote: Under 90 seconds is the automated canonical run. Flagged diffs still get human review — the suite removed the undifferentiated reading, not the judgement.

regression_suite_runtime.label: Full CI regression suite
regression_suite_runtime.basis: Stages 1–3 measured from execution reports; the current figure (22–24 min) is recalled from Allure observation rather than an archived report, so it is stated as ~23.
regression_suite_runtime.scopeNote: Not one optimisation. Serial Robot → pabot with one-login-per-worker (39 min) → suite growth eroded it back to ~65 min → Playwright with 6-way sharding plus moving ~28% of UI scenarios to the API level.

ci_smoke_runtime.basis: Jenkins build timestamps for the Robot stages; Playwright/Allure CI reports for the current figure.

platform_scale.display: 6 countries · 6+ AI product lines · 1 QA engineer
platform_scale.label: What the evaluation systems cover
platform_scale.basis: India, Indonesia, Thailand, Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda. QA consolidated to a single engineer in October 2025.
platform_scale.scopeNote: This is scope of responsibility, not personal achievement. It is the honest way to carry the platform's user numbers: I am accountable for quality across them, I did not build them.

countries.basis: India, Indonesia, Thailand, Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda.
countries.role: quality and evaluation across all six
countries.scopeNote: The '3' that appears in older copy was an HPV market count (India, Indonesia, Thailand), not a country count. Where three is meant, say 'three HPV markets'.

monthly_users.scopeNote: Scale of the system under test. Never framed as something I delivered.

registered_users_2m.unpublishedReason: A cumulative registration total next to a monthly-active figure invites the reader to treat them as the same quantity, and the larger number is the one that sticks. One scale figure sitewide: monthly users.

coverage_zero_to_seventyfive.basis: Observed from suite growth against total test-case count over 2022–2025.
coverage_zero_to_seventyfive.unpublishedReason: The single riskiest claim on the old site. 'Coverage' is undefined here — it is neither line coverage nor requirement coverage — the denominator moved constantly, and the figure has not been re-measured since the suite passed 225 scenarios. It reads as precise and is not. The coverage story is told qualitatively instead, or through suite size, which is countable.

playwright_scenarios.basis: Suite size, counted. 225+ end-2024, 280+ early 2025, 300+ mid-2026.
playwright_scenarios.scopeNote: Growth came from new country variants, dashboard modules and visual regression — not a 1:1 port of the Robot suite.

api_endpoints.basis: Counted across conversation, user, session/state, NLP classifier and referral services.

regression_effort_days.display: 5 → 2 people-days of manual regression per release
regression_effort_days.basis: Team-level estimate across release cycles, self-tracked. Not drawn from a time-tracking system.
regression_effort_days.scopeNote: Stated with its base rather than as '60% reduction'. A percentage without a denominator is unfalsifiable; five days to two is checkable.

post_release_defects.basis: Sprint retrospective defect records, comparing roughly a quarter of sprints before QA sign-off gates against roughly a quarter after. The exact sprint count in each window is not recalled.

e2e_latency_2026.basis: Release timing comparison across the 15 June 2026 release.
e2e_latency_2026.role: benchmarking and evaluation, not the retrieval architecture
e2e_latency_2026.scopeNote: The regression that produced the 28.3s figure lived in staging and never reached production users. Two changes shipped together — reranker removal and a generator-model upgrade — so the improvement cannot be attributed to either alone.

reranker_batching_share.unit: share of the RAG retrieval latency reduction attributable to one fix
reranker_batching_share.basis: Component micro-benchmark (March 2026) put it at ~83%; a contemporaneous independent account put it at ~84%. The two agree within a percentage point.
reranker_batching_share.credit: an engineer on the pipeline team
reranker_batching_share.role: I benchmarked and validated the improvement; I did not implement it
reranker_batching_share.scopeNote: Mandatory context wherever RAG latency improvement is mentioned. Collapsing 20 sequential cross-encoder inference calls into one batched tensor pass accounts for the overwhelming majority of it. Omitting this credit would make the latency work read as mine.

pact_blast_radius.unit: BigQuery event rows that would have carried a fallback intent instead of a safety classification
pact_blast_radius.basis: Historical traffic replayed through the refactored classifier.
pact_blast_radius.footnote: This is a replay projection for a change that never shipped, not an observed production count. The contract verification stopped it before staging.

pact_provider_states.basis: Pact Broker verification run records. The two safety-category interactions failed; the other seven passed.
pact_provider_states.scopeNote: The precision is the argument: a schema diff passed this change because the JSON stayed valid. Only a consumer-expectation check could fail exactly the two interactions that mattered.

security_scan_first_pass.display: two high-severity findings in the first authenticated scan, both fixed within the sprint
security_scan_first_pass.basis: First structured DAST pass over the platform.
security_scan_first_pass.scopeNote: Deliberately qualitative. The full finding breakdown is a map of where to look at a client system and is not publishable; the finding classes are not named on the site either.

judge_agreement_geval.basis: Tone Appropriateness criterion, measured against a 30-example annotated calibration set before and after adding concrete PASS/FAIL example pairs.
judge_agreement_geval.credit: the health content team, who annotated the calibration set

judge_calibration_set.basis: Calibration set for the redesigned Smart Snippets judge. Rule: rewrite the criteria whenever disagreement exceeds 15%.
judge_calibration_set.credit: the health content team, who annotated the set

ragas_embedding_swap_catch.basis: Nightly RAGAS CI job results artefact. An embedding-model swap reached staging tested only for latency and memory; the danger-sign recognition category dropped before manual QA started for the sprint.

cache_eval_set.basis: Pulled from Indonesia and India production logs over a 14-day window and labelled by hand.

cache_precision_recall.basis: Measured against thresholds of ≥0.90 precision and ≥0.75 recall.
cache_precision_recall.scopeNote: The asymmetric thresholds are the point: a cache miss falls through safely to live generation, a false cache hit serves a wrong answer. The two errors are not worth the same, so they are not gated the same.

cache_regression_catch.basis: A staging run ahead of a classification-schema change dropped below the 0.90 gate and blocked the deploy; a re-run after the fix passed at 0.94.

anomaly_sampling_yield.display: 3–4× more judge-worthy edge cases per week at the same cost
anomaly_sampling_yield.basis: My own framing over the pipeline's first month of operation, comparing anomaly-triggered oversampling layered on 5% uniform hash sampling against uniform sampling alone. Not an instrumented measurement.

clinical_safety_pass.unit: Clinical Safety PASS rate on the India Maternal Health production sample
clinical_safety_pass.basis: Production monitoring evaluation pipeline, after the danger-sign fix shipped.

danger_sign_fix_time.display: two weeks from pipeline go-live to a shipped fix
danger_sign_fix_time.basis: Pipeline operational logs. The fix was retrieval query augmentation, a prompt rule, and 12 new golden-dataset cases.
danger_sign_fix_time.scopeNote: The failure mode was invisible to golden-dataset regression, the conversational suite, RAGAS Faithfulness and manual spot-checks — four independent layers. That is the finding, not the two weeks.

annotation_override_rate.display: 20% of Clinical Safety FAIL verdicts overridden by human annotators
annotation_override_rate.basis: First annotation cycle with the health content team, in progress at the time of writing.
annotation_override_rate.scopeNote: Published as a limitation, not a result. It says the judge is too conservative on non-urgent symptom mentions because the criteria do not distinguish severity.

framework_reuse_velocity.unit: from 'chatbot ready for evaluation' to 'nightly evaluation job live'
framework_reuse_velocity.basis: My own comparison across the three HPV launches, which reused the runner, judge, calibration pipeline, nightly job and results table and needed only dataset curation.

crisis_prompt_fp_testset.display: 13 → 5 false positives across 32 fixed test cases
crisis_prompt_fp_testset.basis: Before/after comparison on a fixed regression test set through the evaluation framework. True-positive detection stayed at 100% in both versions.
crisis_prompt_fp_testset.scopeNote: The unchanged true-positive rate is the load-bearing half. Cutting false positives on a safety classifier is worthless if it costs recall.

crisis_prompt_fp_production.display: 45% reduction in the production false-positive rate
crisis_prompt_fp_production.basis: Production monitoring over the two sprints following release.

unnecessary_llm_invocations.basis: Manual analysis of input-classifier traffic logs, February 2026. Roughly 18 points of it was acknowledgement-type input with vocabulary gaps; the rest was gibberish, emoji and menu selections.

visual_regression.display: 28 scenarios at 0.2% pixel tolerance, 3 regressions caught in 6 months
visual_regression.basis: Direct count and CI timing data. Overhead is roughly 200–400ms per scenario.

robot_retirement_ported.basis: 8 in a proof of concept, then 39 in the full port. Zero result divergence across a full parallel-run release cycle before the Robot job and image were decommissioned.

ci_flake_rate.basis: Jenkins build history, September to November 2022. Vue components became visible in the DOM before their content finished loading, so a visibility wait alone was insufficient.

docker_setup_time.unit: to stand up a test environment on a new machine
docker_setup_time.basis: My own before/after observation around Docker adoption. Not timed formally.

stt_latency.basis: Benchmarked across the same Assamese audio set through both providers.

stt_duration_banded_collapse.basis: The losing provider held 100% clean output on short clips and collapsed to 30% on 15–25 second clips — the duration band real users actually send. Only visible once the analysis was banded by audio duration instead of aggregated.
stt_duration_banded_collapse.scopeNote: The single best argument on the site for disaggregating a metric before trusting it.

voice_vs_text_length.basis: 203 transcribed voice queries against 405 typed queries, India Maternal Health.

voice_vs_text_noise.basis: Same 203-voice / 405-text sample. Noise is filler or pure acknowledgement with no clinical substance.

pypi_downloads.basis: PyPI stats including mirror traffic, which inflates the figure by an unknown amount. 391 in the trailing 30 days at time of measurement.

engineers_upskilled.basis: One senior engineer with no prior automation experience, mentored through a structured learning path, plus two campus recruits through a four-month programme.

_superseded.correction: 6 countries. The three was an HPV market count (India, Indonesia, Thailand), not a country count.
Restated with its base as 5 → 2 people-days per release. See regression_effort_days.
Not published in any form. See security_scan_first_pass.
Not published. Softened to the qualitative statement in security_scan_first_pass.
